setup.data: Repetition: 2,736 response-level records (1,368 repetitive from a 928,046-entry pool, 1,368 non-repetitive all-judge-true), prompts not matched across classes. Sycophancy: DataCreatorAI/Anti-Sycophancy-DPO, 3,480 chosen(truthful)/rejected(sycophantic) pairs on user claims such as 'All smartphones are spying on us all the time.'; responses are teacher-forced dataset text, not the model's own generations; a 'stance span' is extracted from each response by Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (6,678 of 6,960 records kept). Post-training data: repetition 755,920 SFT records / DPO pairs (repaired continuations written by Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct); sycophancy 3,480 SFT examples / 3,480 DPO pairs from the same Anti-Sycophancy-DPO source.
setup.models_and_sizes: Atlas: 23 models from Gemma (2-2B, 2-2B-it, 3-4B-it, 2-9B, 2-9B-it, 2-27B, 2-27B-it), Qwen (2.5-0.5B, 0.5B-Instruct, 7B, 7B-Instruct, 2.5-32B, 32B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-27B), Mistral (7B-v0.3, 7B-Instruct, Nemo base/instruct, Small-3.1-24B base/instruct), Llama (3.1-8B, 3.1-8B-Instruct, 3.3-70B-Instruct). Controlled post-training: only Llama-3.1-8B base, one seed (42).
setup.layers_positions: Features are MLP down_proj inputs (FFN intermediate neurons) in all layers, flattened (e.g. 32 x 14,336 = 458,752 for Llama-3.1-8B), mean-pooled over a behavior span (sycophancy: extracted stance-text tokens; repetition: repeated span). NOC as implemented is |activation| x column norm of W_down / ||layer output||, a non-negative magnitude proxy. Sparse L1 logistic regression (C=1, saga) picks positive-weight coordinates (BACs: 20-61 for repetition, 42-101 for sycophancy); chart = PCA to 90% variance. Sycophancy classifier is 3-vs-1: positive = stance tokens of sycophantic records; negative = stance tokens of truthful records plus all non-stance tokens of both.
setup.post_training_protocol: Six runs per behavior from Llama-3.1-8B: SFT-up, SFT-down, DPO-up and DPO-down from base, SFT->DPO-up and SFT->DPO-down. SFT lr 1e-5 (sycophancy: 120 steps ~4.4 epochs up, 360 steps ~13.2 epochs down; repetition: 100 steps up, 600 steps down); DPO lr 5e-7, 60 steps (~2.2 epochs for sycophancy, but only ~0.010 epoch for repetition: 60 x 128 / 755,920 pairs), beta 0.1 (0.7 for SFT->DPO-down sycophancy); DPO reference model = frozen copy of the DPO initialisation. Effective batch 128, fp16, ZeRO-3, seed 42. Ten matched relative stages per run. Behaviour column in Table 2b is p_b/m_b: probability assigned to the behaviour-positive (sycophantic) target / sycophantic preference score. Base-model behaviour values are not reported; the first stored checkpoints (SFT step 10, DPO step 6) sit at sycophancy preference ~0.454 and Syco Prob 0.355.
setup.baselines: Matched-size random coordinate scaffolds (same model and layer distribution) for PCA, CCA, linear probing and steering; base model chart as anchor for post-training; public Base vs Instruct pairs (10 pairs) as uncontrolled ecological check.
setup.controls: Random-coordinate controls (reported numbers for CCA and probing); mean CCA and full-chart probing instead of primary CCA alone; anchored Fisher retention (base chart applied to checkpoint features vs checkpoint's native chart); dose-response steering with PPL tracking for repetition; base-anchored teacher-forced fixed candidate pairs across checkpoints (4 pairs). Label-permutation, rank-sensitivity, token-window and behavior-mismatch controls are described in Appendix I but no numbers for them are given in the text.

key_results.claim: DPO from base keeps the behavior chart; SFT moves it. (Checker caveat: ~9 deg of DPO's ~10 deg sycophancy angle is already present at step 6 for both up and down, so the DPO number is near the measurement floor.)
key_results.quote: Across the four behavior–direction settings, DPO initialized from Base is consistently geometry-conservative, retaining mean projector overlap 0.939 with mean angle 7.64◦

key_results.claim: SFT displaces the chart about 3x more in angle.
key_results.quote: SFT produces substantially larger chart displacement, with mean overlap 0.745 and mean angle 25.07◦

key_results.claim: DPO after SFT stays in the SFT geometry.
key_results.quote: DPO after SFT does not restore the Base chart, indicating that the sequential objective continues optimization within the SFT-induced geometry.

key_results.claim: The 'reweighting' mechanism for DPO is not directly measured: DPO changes all three measured axes only a little.
key_results.quote: In particular, reward-only changes are usually modest in all three measured axes, so the figures support geometric conservation more directly than a universal large occupancy- or gain-shift account.

key_results.claim: Reward-only sycophancy runs barely change behavior.
key_results.quote: Reward-only sycophancy trajectories preserve geometry while moving behavior modestly.

key_results.claim: Leaving the base chart does not mean less sycophancy.
key_results.quote: A trajectory that leaves the high-density Base support does not necessarily indicate weaker sycophancy.

key_results.claim: After SFT, sycophancy rises while paths move away from the base positive direction (the base chart stops being the right coordinate system).
key_results.quote: The fact that sycophantic preference can increase while the corresponding path moves away from the Base positive direction is particularly informative.

key_results.claim: Public instruct models usually have more, not less, causal gain on the repetition chart.
key_results.quote: This pattern is inconsistent with a simple account in which instruction alignment merely suppresses the behavior mechanism.

key_results.claim: Lower separability does not imply lower causal readout.
key_results.quote: This again shows that suppressing statistical separability does not necessarily suppress the causal readout of the behavior.

key_results.claim: Primary CCA alone is not evidence of a shared axis.
key_results.quote: The random primary scores of 0.667 in ACT and 0.817 in NOC are too large to regard a single canonical correlation as decisive evidence.

key_results.claim: Behavior-selected coordinates beat random on mean CCA.
key_results.quote: The ACT score increases from 0.222 under random selection to 0.515 under behavior-associated selection, an absolute increase of 0.293.

key_results.claim: Repetition steering works in all 23 models.
key_results.quote: Both operators produce a positive endpoint behavioral change for every model.

key_results.claim: Public instruct models usually have more causal gain on the repetition chart: 7 of 10 pairs in both NOC and ACT; reliability changes split 5/5 (NOC) and 4/6 (ACT).
key_results.quote: Seven of ten pairs exhibit positive changes in NOC causal gain, and seven of ten exhibit positive changes in ACT causal gain.

methods.name: Sparse behavior-coordinate scaffold + PCA chart (ACT and NOC)
methods.what_it_measures: L1-logistic selection of MLP neurons that predict a behavior label, then a low-rank PCA basis U of those neurons' pooled activations (ACT) or magnitude-normalized contributions (NOC).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Gives the subspace to track; ACT-vs-NOC split (present vs functionally contributing) is a weak screen for bypass (fate 2): coordinates active but with little contribution to the layer update.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Neuron scaling and chart-subspace add/remove steering on the selected coordinates.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Few thousand labeled examples; forward passes with hooks on down_proj; sklearn L1 logistic on up to ~460k features per model (8B).

methods.name: Grassmannian chart tracking across checkpoints
methods.what_it_measures: Projector overlap S, mean principal angle, projection distance between base and checkpoint charts at matched rank; velocity, path length and excess path length over checkpoints.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Transformed (fate 5): chart rotates after a fix; vs retained geometry (fate 1/4 style readout or competition change).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Steer along base vs new chart at the new checkpoint to see which one still controls behavior.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Charts at each checkpoint (one forward pass per checkpoint over the item set); cheap linear algebra.

methods.name: Anchored Fisher retention R^G
methods.what_it_measures: Fisher separability of checkpoint features projected into the base chart, divided by separability in the checkpoint's own chart.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Stage B removed vs hidden: R^G ~1 with behavior fixed = old code still there and readable (hidden); R^G << 1 with native G high = re-encoded (transformed); both low = erased (fate 6). Also a direct H3 test: does a pre-fix probe still work post-fix.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Patch base-chart component back in post-fix to test whether behavior returns.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Same as above; needs labels at each checkpoint.

methods.name: Geometry / occupancy / gain / threshold decomposition
methods.what_it_measures: Chart movement (d_proj), class-conditional second-moment occupancy gap G_occ, finite-difference causal gain G_causal from steering, intercept tau from logistic fit.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Readout/threshold failure (fate 1: gain or intercept change with geometry fixed) vs override (fate 4: occupancy shift) vs transformed (geometry move).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Gain is itself causal (dose-response); threshold term is said to be estimable but no tau values are reported.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Steering sweeps at 5 strengths per checkpoint per model.

methods.name: Cross-model CCA atlas with random-coordinate control
methods.what_it_measures: Primary and mean canonical correlation between two models' chart coordinates on matched items; directed linear probing; same with matched random coordinates.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Not a fate test; tells whether a fate-relevant axis found at 9B is the same axis at 27B.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Same item set run through every model.

methods.name: Base-anchored teacher-forced candidate paths
methods.what_it_measures: For fixed prompt + truthful and sycophantic candidate answers, token-by-token projections into the base chart at each checkpoint, with length-normalized likelihood as node size.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Per-item view of Stage B: does the fix move items out of the old chart (transformed) or keep them inside while changing preference (readout/override)?
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Natural place to patch base-checkpoint states into the post-fix model per item.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Teacher-forced passes of paired candidates at each checkpoint; trivial compute.

methods.name: Token-level trajectories over log-density-ratio landscape
methods.what_it_measures: Per-token chart coordinates plotted over log p+(z)/p-(z) background.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Where flipped vs resisted items split along the answer (group angle: token paths).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Choose the token position for patching.

controls_worth_copying: Matched-size random coordinate scaffolds from the same layers, run through the whole pipeline (PCA, CCA, probing, steering).
Report mean CCA and full-chart probing, not primary CCA (random primary CCA reached 0.667 ACT / 0.817 NOC).
Anchored retention: apply the pre-fix chart to post-fix activations and compare with the post-fix native chart.
Track every checkpoint, not only endpoints (rules out 'moves then returns').
Same prompts and same teacher-forced candidates across all checkpoints, plotted in base coordinates.
Dose-response steering with PPL tracked, and local finite-difference gain instead of endpoint differences.
Separate discovery data from post-training data (they checked overlap: 39 exact matches in the first 100k).

pitfalls.pitfall: Update size and behavior change are not matched between SFT and DPO: DPO uses lr 5e-7 for 60 steps vs SFT lr 1e-5 for 100-600 steps; repetition DPO sees only ~1% of its data (0.010 epoch); sycophancy DPO moves Syco Prob by about 0.015. 'Geometry preserved' may just mean 'little changed'.
pitfalls.quote: In particular, reward-only changes are usually modest in all three measured axes, so the figures support geometric conservation more directly than a universal large occupancy- or gain-shift account.

pitfalls.pitfall: Sycophancy SFT runs are many epochs on 3,480 examples (high overfit), DPO about 2 epochs.
pitfalls.quote: SFT-up runs for 120 steps (∼4.4 effective epochs) and SFT-down for 360 steps (∼13.2 effective epochs).

pitfalls.pitfall: NOC as implemented is an unsigned magnitude proxy, not the signed contribution defined in Section 3.3, so it cannot show opposing/cancelling contributions.
pitfalls.quote: The implemented proxy is non-negative and does not preserve the sign or direction of an individual coordinate's contribution.

pitfalls.pitfall: L1 coordinate selection on unstandardized features.
pitfalls.quote: Because L1 regularization is not scale-invariant, the coordinate selection described below may be influenced by the relative scales of the per-neuron features.

pitfalls.pitfall: 3-vs-1 classifier: non-stance tokens of both classes are negatives, so selected neurons can partly code 'stance span vs rest of text', not sycophancy.
pitfalls.quote: Other-region features from sycophantic records (negative, label 0): activation vectors from all_except_answer_tokens for _rejected records.

pitfalls.pitfall: The chart is a PCA of the scaffold, not a discriminant subspace. In ACT the sycophancy PC1 is nearly orthogonal to the classifier direction (mean signed cosine 0.062, several 0.000, across the 23 atlas models), so the dominant chart direction is not the behaviour direction; the behaviour direction may sit in lower PCs. Chart rotation therefore need not mean the behaviour direction rotated (and vice versa).
pitfalls.quote: denotes the reported signed cosine similarity between PC1 and the supervised classifier direction.

pitfalls.pitfall: Sycophancy labels come from a fixed preference dataset of user opinions/claims, teacher-forced; no model-generated flips and no check of what the model itself believes.
pitfalls.quote: We constructed the sycophancy data from DataCreatorAI/Anti-Sycophancy-DPO, which provides 3 480 chosen–rejected preference pairs.

pitfalls.pitfall: Public Base vs Instruct comparisons are confounded.
pitfalls.quote: The comparison is paired at the model-family and parameter-scale level, but it is not a controlled training intervention.

pitfalls.pitfall: Discovery and intervention prompts not fully disjoint.
pitfalls.quote: Because this audit covered only a subset of the intervention corpus, we do not claim strict prompt-level disjointness.

pitfalls.pitfall: Layer counts of selected neurons are not causal importance.
pitfalls.quote: they should not be interpreted as direct measurements of layer-wise causal importance.

pitfalls.pitfall: Repetition DPO is ~0.010 epoch, so the repetition 'reward preserves geometry' result rests on a tiny update.
pitfalls.quote: All DPO runs complete 60 optimization steps, corresponding to an effective epoch count of ∼0.010 (60 × 128 / 755 920).

pitfalls.pitfall: Measurement floor not reported: DPO-up and DPO-down sycophancy are identical at step 6 (S 0.9498, 9.06 deg, Syco Prob 0.3550) and the SFT first checkpoint also sits at ~9 deg, so ~9 deg / S~0.95 looks like a floor from chart re-estimation or checkpoint conversion. There is no base-vs-base (re-extraction or seed) control for S or angle. After step 6, DPO moves <=1 deg.
pitfalls.quote: Behavior moves gradually, but overlap remains around 0.94–0.95.

pitfalls.pitfall: Per-checkpoint chart pipeline may re-fit the sparse classifier and neuron set ('train or reuse'), then zero-pad bases to a common ambient space; it is not stated which checkpoints reuse the base mask, so S and angle mix neuron re-selection with representation change.
pitfalls.quote: extract activations for the base and checkpoint, train or reuse sparse classifiers, extract selected neurons, compute global padded indices, run PCA, zero-pad bases to a common ambient coordinate system

pitfalls.pitfall: The two sycophancy behaviour metrics disagree for SFT-down: p_b (prob. of sycophantic target) rises to 0.442 vs 0.355 at the first DPO checkpoint, while the preference score falls to 0.330. Base-model behaviour is never reported.
pitfalls.quote: The Behavior entry reports pb /mb , where pb is the evaluation probability assigned to the behavior-positive target and mb is the realized behavioral metric.

pitfalls.pitfall: Overclaim in the headline: Figure 1 and the abstract say reward optimization redistributes occupancy and changes readout gain or threshold, but threshold is never estimated and Appendix S finds occupancy and gain changes for DPO are small and estimator-dependent.
pitfalls.quote: whereas reward-based optimization largely preserves the inherited chart while redistributing occupancy and modifying readout gain or threshold

pitfalls.pitfall: Internal inconsistencies: Table 2a random baselines (0.367/0.317 primary CCA) conflict with Table 15 (0.667/0.817); Figure 5a repetition values do not match Table 2b; Table 6 Truth PPL 1485.1 vs Table 2b 1.48; Table 7 up/down step-6 rows identical; Figure 11/13 PC1 25.5% vs Table 4 Llama-3.1-8B ACT PC1 0.426; Figure 5d SFT axis ends at 120 steps while SFT-down ran 360. Single model, single seed, no confidence intervals; Appendix I robustness controls described without reported numbers.

limitations_quote: geometric conservation versus movement, but they do not by themselves prove which non-geometric mechanism causes the remaining behavioral change.
limitations_extra: No dedicated limitations section. Other admitted gaps: 'Threshold changes, subtle readout reconfiguration, or distributional changes outside the second-moment occupancy statistic remain plausible mechanisms' (p45); repaired repetition continuations not re-checked for repetition (p60); public pairs confounded (p41).
future_work_quote: None stated (no future-work section; the paper ends at a two-sentence conclusion on p7-8).

bears_on_fates.how: Closest prior method for the recheck: track the pre-fix subspace across fix checkpoints with principal angles + anchored retention. Their sycophancy-down DPO keeps the base chart (S 0.939, R^G 0.995) while behavior barely moves (Syco Prob 0.355 -> 0.342), consistent with 'hidden/reweighted, not removed', but the behavior change is too small to call it a fix, and ~9 of the 9.68 deg is a first-checkpoint offset shared with DPO-up, so 'conserved' is not distinguished from 'unchanged'.

SFT rotates the chart by 22-31 deg; in Figure 13 SFT moves both truthful and sycophantic candidates out of the base chart's positive/negative separation while sycophantic preference rises, i.e. behavior re-encoded in new coordinates. 4 items, qualitative.
Decomposition defines gain (slope) and intercept (threshold) inside a fixed chart; public instruct models gain causal readout while separability drops. Threshold values never reported.
ACT-high / NOC-low quadrant = active but little functional contribution; only conceptual, NOC is an unsigned proxy.
Occupancy shift inside a kept chart is their stand-in; no competing-signal analysis.
Native Fisher G stays high after every run (10-18 for sycophancy), so no erasure observed; R^G with native G gives the test.

bears_on_group_angle: Directly uses Grassmannian tools the group wants (projector overlap, principal angles, projection distance, path length/velocity over checkpoints) but over training time, not across layers: the chart concatenates selected neurons from all layers, so there is no layer-by-layer subspace path. No Procrustes (only CCA, which is not orthogonal). Token-path idea is present (Appendix K, L: teacher-forced candidate paths in a fixed base chart) but on 4 pairs with no flipped-vs-resisted split and no matching on prior confidence. No attention heads (MLP neurons only).
bears_on_H1_H2_H3: H1: not tested (one pressure type: user states an opinion/claim; no pushback-after-answer or tempting-option conditions). H2: not tested (only SFT and DPO, up/down; no fate-matched fix). Their result predicts plain DPO leaves the inherited geometry in place, which is the premise of H2's 'plain DPO hides' arm, but with unmatched update size and DPO movement near the measurement floor. H3: anchored retention is a direct analogue: base-chart separability survives DPO (R^G 0.995-0.998) and mostly survives SFT (0.81-0.97), arguing that old probes keep working at the population level; Figure 13 shows per-item cases where the old chart stops separating after SFT, which is the H3 failure mode, but only 4 items. Caveat: R^G labels are fixed dataset labels on teacher-forced text (sycophantic vs truthful response), not the model's own behaviour, so it tests whether an old probe still separates the same text, not whether it catches the model's failures (our H3).
overlap_with_our_plan: DOES: (1) asks the same Stage B question in general form ('remove, build a competing mechanism, rotate, shift occupancy, weaken readout'); (2) tracks a sycophancy subspace through controlled SFT, DPO and SFT->DPO checkpoints on Llama-3.1-8B with principal angles, projector overlap and anchored retention; (3) claims SFT rewrites and DPO reweights; (4) separates geometry, occupancy and causal gain. LEAVES OPEN: (a) no decodable correct answer: sycophancy is 'sycophantic vs truthful stance text' on opinion claims, so no knowing-vs-acting gap, no probe for the correct answer, no 'decodable but flipped' items; (b) no per-item fates and no six-way sort (Stage A untouched); (c) no fate-matched fixes, no H2; (d) only Llama-3.1-8B, one seed, DPO with 20x smaller lr and ~no behavior change, so 'DPO hides' is not established; (e) no pressure types (H1); (f) MLP neurons only, no attention heads reading the user claim, no layerwise subspace path, no Procrustes transformed-vs-erased test; (g) sycophancy chart causal validation is weak (NOC gain mean 0.062, sometimes negative; steering curves only for repetition); (h) no base-vs-base noise floor: DPO's ~10 deg is mostly a ~9 deg first-checkpoint offset shared by DPO-up, DPO-down and SFT, so 'DPO reweights' is weaker than the headline; (i) R^G uses fixed dataset labels, not the model's own flips. Scoop risk for Stage B: moderate on framing ('rewrite vs reweight' for SFT vs DPO on sycophancy geometry is now taken and must be cited), low on substance (removal vs hiding of a decodable correct answer, per item, with fate-matched fixes and matched update size is not done).
architecture_location: MLP down_proj inputs (FFN intermediate neurons), all layers concatenated; in Llama-3.1-8B the sycophancy scaffold is broad (nearly all 32 layers) with peaks around middle (~layer 13) and late (~layer 23, ~27) layers (approx, read from Figure 14; the paper warns counts are not causal importance); repetition scaffold is sparse. No attention components are analysed.
actionable_fix: No sycophancy fix is proposed or shown. Implied: if a fix should change the mechanism rather than reweight it, SFT moves the chart far more than DPO; DPO after SFT stays in the SFT geometry, so the order of stages matters. Repetition can be raised by ACT-chart steering in all 23 models (repetition is the only behavior with demonstrated causal control).
reuse_verdict: Reuse the measurement kit for Stage B: matched-rank principal angles + projector overlap across fix checkpoints, anchored retention R^G (pre-fix probe on post-fix model vs post-fix native probe), checkpoint-by-checkpoint trajectories, base-anchored teacher-forced paired candidates, random-coordinate controls. Do not copy: unsigned NOC proxy, unstandardized L1 selection, 3-vs-1 span labels, PCA-of-scaffold chart whose PC1 is orthogonal to the behavior direction (use a supervised or class-difference subspace instead), and unmatched SFT vs DPO budgets (match KL or behavior change before comparing geometry).
